10.14.7.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa Thus the wisdom of God saved the people by accepting the crucifixion, so that the people might be crucified with Him, and rise with Him in surpassing glory, and the true believers might be made worthy of heaven.

10.14.8.en: Pharaoh humbled the people and forced them to labor in clay and in the building of three cities, enslaving them. In this he represents the work of the enemy of good with mankind, the sons of Adam.

10.14.9.en: * Pharaoh enslaved the children of Israel in building cities for himself. Pharaoh appointed taskmasters from among his soldiers over the children of Israel, urging them on to his works. And the devil appoints demons over the sons of Adam, urging them on to his evil works, the works of sin.

10.14.10.en: Pharaoh appointed his soldiers to enslave the children of Israel to the making of bricks, and the devil urges the sons of Adam on to lowly earthly works.

10.14.11.en: The Holy Scripture mentions that the children of Israel built great cities for Pharaoh (Ex 1:11)... And the demons urge the sons of Adam to set up great sins that are the root of all evils: the love of silver, the lusts of the flesh, and vainglory.

10.14.12.en: St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian Truly, what do we expect from the earthy heart of Pharaoh, filled with mire, except that he should issue orders to force the children of Israel into the work of clay?

10.14.13.en: * For Satan, who harms people and corrupts them, is intensely concerned that his subjects should not look up to heaven, but should bow down to the earth and make bricks of clay - within themselves - from the mud. And it is clear to everyone that what belongs to material pleasure is certainly composed of earth and water, and this applies to the one who is concerned with the lust for food or the lust for money and wealth.

10.14.14.en: The mixture of these two elements - earth and water - becomes clay. And those who long for pleasures are like those who long for clay; they keep filling themselves with it, and yet they are never filled, and the place that receives the clay becomes empty before the next pouring. In the same way the brickmaker keeps pouring more clay into the mold, and the mold is continually emptied. Everyone can easily understand the meaning of this figure by looking at the sensual side of the soul.

10.14.15.en: Whoever follows his desires and what he craves, if he achieves one desire and then turns with his desire to something else, finds himself empty again with respect to that thing; and if he is filled with it, he becomes empty again like an empty vessel, seeking something else, and so on. And we do not cease from this until we depart from this material life.

10.14.16.en: As for the straw and the chaff that those subject to the tyrant's orders had to mix with the bricks, both the holy Gospel and the lofty voice of the Apostle (Paul) explain them as materials for burning (Ezek 5:4; Mt 3:12).

10.15.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa She entered into the soul of the servant of the Lord, and withstood dreadful kings with wonders and signs. [16]

10.15.1.en: If the wisdom of God raised up Moses the prophet as a leader for the salvation of his people, then the secret of the power is not in the person of Moses, but in the wisdom of God that entered into his soul because he was the servant of the Lord. The resistance to Pharaoh and the men of his army was not from the human wisdom of Moses, nor his plans, nor his abilities, but it was "the wisdom of God" that repelled the continual assaults.

10.15.2.en: What happened with Moses the prophet to accomplish the Exodus was a type of the accomplishment of an exodus from the captivity of the devil into the divine embrace. It is a type of what the believers in Christ Jesus, the Savior of the world, enjoy, and of their surpassing victory over the devil and his kingdom.

10.15.3.en: And the signs and wonders that were accomplished, such as the ten plagues, were the work of the wisdom of God. And the means of enjoying the work of wisdom is faith together with prayer.

10.15.4.en: The use of the plural indicates the resistance of the kings surrounding them during their wandering in the wilderness, besides the resistance of Pharaoh to them while they were in Egypt and immediately after their departure. Perhaps by the kings he means the rulers of the provinces of Egypt.

10.15.5.en: * By the Passover these came out of the bondage of Pharaoh, and we, on the day of the crucifixion, are delivered from the bondage of Satan.

10.15.6.en: They slew a lamb from the flock, and by its blood they were saved from the destroyer, and we were saved by the blood of a chosen Son from the works of corruption that we have done.

10.15.7.en: They had Moses as a leader, and we have Jesus as a guide and Savior.

10.15.8.en: Moses divided the sea for them and made them pass through, but our Savior broke open Hades and shattered its gates, and entered within and opened them. And He marked out the way before all who believe in Him.

10.15.9.en: Moses gave them water from the rock, and our Savior caused living water to flow for us from His breast.

10.15.10.en: Moses promised them the land of the Canaanites as an inheritance, and our Lord promised us the land of life as a kingdom.

10.15.11.en: Moses lifted up a serpent of brass; everyone who looked at it remained alive in spite of the bite of the serpent. And Jesus hung Himself up, and everyone who looks to Him is saved from the wound of the serpent, who is Satan.

10.15.12.en: Moses made for them the temporary tabernacle in which to offer sacrifices and offerings, that they might be cleansed from their sins. And Jesus raised up the tabernacle of David that is fallen down (Amos 9:10; Acts 15:16), and rose. And He said to the Jews: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up" (Jn 2:19). And His disciples understood that He spoke of His body, which He raises after three days when they kill Him. For in this tabernacle He promised us life, and by it our sins are cleansed.

10.15.13.en: He called their tabernacle a temporary tabernacle, because it served for a short time, and He called our tabernacle the temple of the Holy Spirit, which endures forever (1 Cor 3:16; 6:19).

10.15.14.en: * Moses brought his people out of the service of Pharaoh, and Jesus delivered the nations from the service of Satan.

10.15.15.en: Moses was brought up in the house of Pharaoh, and Jesus was brought up in Egypt when Joseph fled with Him there.

10.15.16.en: Miriam stood on the edge of the river when Moses floated on the water, and Mary conceived Jesus when the angel Gabriel gave her the good news.

10.15.17.en: When Moses slew the lamb, the firstborn of the Egyptians were killed, and Jesus became the true Lamb when they crucified Him, and by His death the murderous people died.

10.15.18.en: Moses brought down manna for his people, and Jesus gave His body to the nations.

10.15.19.en: With a tree Moses sweetened the bitter waters, and by His cross Jesus sweetened our bitterness with the wood of the tree of His cross.

10.15.20.en: Moses brought down the Law for his people, and Jesus gave His covenants to the nations.

10.15.21.en: Moses conquered Amalek when he stretched out his hands, and Jesus conquered Satan by the sign of the cross.

10.15.22.en: Moses brought forth waters from the rock for his people, and Jesus sent Simon Cephas to carry His teaching among the nations.

10.15.23.en: Moses lifted the veil from his face and spoke with God, and Jesus took the veil away from the face of the nations so that they might hear His teaching and receive it.

10.15.24.en: Moses laid his hand on his apostles and they received the priesthood, and Jesus laid His hand on His apostles and they received the Holy Spirit.

10.15.25.en: Moses went up the mountain and died there, and Jesus ascended to heaven and sat at the right hand of the Father.

10.15.26.en: St. Aphrahat the Persian Sage * When Moses saw that all the people (the Egyptians) agreed with their leader (Pharaoh) in his evil, he struck all the Egyptians with a plague, and no one escaped the calamities (Ex 7:17 etc.). And all the elements of the universe - earth, water, air and fire, which enter into everything that exists - cooperated with him in this attack on the Egyptians, as though they were an army carrying out orders, and these elements changed their natural laws to serve human purposes. For at the same time, in the same place and with the same force, sinners were being punished while those who were not sinners suffered nothing.

10.16.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa She rendered to the saints a reward of their labors, and guided them in a wondrous way, and was a shelter to them by day, and a light of stars in the night. [17]

10.16.1.en: Here he points even to the material recompense, in that they took the precious things belonging to the Egyptians in return for their enslavement and the deprivation of their rights (Ex 3:21-22; 11:2-3; 12:35-36). Perhaps by the recompense he refers to liberation from bondage.

10.16.2.en: "A shelter by day," for the cloud was a guide to them and at the same time a shelter to protect them from the heat of the sun. "And the LORD will create upon every dwelling place of mount Zion, and upon her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night: for upon all the glory shall be a defence. And there shall be a tabernacle for a shadow in the daytime from the heat, and for a place of refuge, and for a covert from storm and from rain" (Isa 4:5-6).

10.16.3.en: Here the wise man explained the appearance of the Lord as a cloud shading them by day and a pillar of fire giving them light and leading them, saying that He is wisdom, or the wisdom of God (who later became incarnate to save the world).

10.16.4.en: * The divine power sent a cloud to lead the people (Ex 13:21-22), and this was not an ordinary cloud, for it was not composed of vapors like ordinary clouds, nor was it a misty formation produced by the pressure of the winds on vapors, but it was something beyond human understanding. And Scripture bears witness that there was something extraordinary in this cloud, for when the rays of the noonday sun shone with intense heat, the cloud was a shelter for the people, casting shade from above and moistening the fiery heat of the air with a light dew. And during the night it was changed into fire leading the Israelites - as in a procession - with its light from sunset to sunrise.

10.17.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa She brought them through the Red Sea, and led them through much water. [18]

10.17.1.en: The way that wisdom chose for the departure from Egypt and the crossing to the land of promise was to bring them through the Red Sea and make them pass through much water. This was not the way according to human logic, since there was an easy and smooth road at that time, the one in the direction of El-Arish, by which they would reach the Jordan directly. No one realized the mystery in this, since it was not possible for them to enter the land of promise except through this way, for the following reasons: 1. The crossing of the Red Sea as a type of the enjoyment of Baptism, so that the believers may cross over to the heavenly Canaan. 2. Entering into tribulations and wars, so that Pharaoh and his soldiers perish as a sign of the destruction of the devil and his angels. And Amalek and other nations are defeated, as they are types of the sins that he must crush by the power of the cross during our striving by the grace of God. 3. The people's remaining forty years so that they might completely forget every experience of idolatry with which they had come into contact in Egypt. 4. So that Moses might die and Joshua take over the leadership, for there is no entering into eternity unless the letter of the Law dies and we live by the Spirit under the leadership of our Lord Jesus (Joshua). 5. The enjoyment of the experience of praise in the midst of the wilderness. 6. The enjoyment of the heavenly manna as a type of partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord. 7. The enjoyment of taking refuge under the wings of the Lord (the cloud) and of being enlightened by His Holy Spirit (the pillar of fire by night).

10.17.2.en: * In that crossing the pillar of cloud was a guide. And those before us did well in interpreting the pillar of cloud as the mercy of the Holy Spirit, who guides those worthy toward the good; and whoever follows the Holy Spirit crosses the waters, since the guide makes a way for him in them, and in this way leads him safely to freedom, but the one who pursues him to bring him back to bondage perishes in the water. Those who hear this must not be ignorant of the mystery of the water. For whoever goes down into the water with the enemy's army comes out alone, leaving the enemy's army to drown in the water.

10.18.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa But their enemies she drowned, and then cast them up from the bottom of the deep. [19]

10.18.1.en: * Moses himself watched the cloud and taught the people how it remained within their sight (Ex 14:16-22). And after the cloud had guided them along their whole course, they reached the Red Sea, where the Egyptians, coming up from behind, surrounded the people with all their army. And there was no escape from this terror available to the Israelites in any direction, for they were hemmed in between their enemies and the water. Then Moses - moved by a divine power - carried out the most marvelous deed, scarcely to be believed at all: he approached the shore and struck the sea with his rod. And the sea was split by the blow, just as a crack that occurs in glass runs from any point to the edge. In this way the whole sea was split from above by the action of the rod, and the cleft ran through the waters until it reached the opposite shore. And in the place where the sea was split, Moses went down into the depth with all the people without being wetted, and their bodies were still bathed in the light of the sun. And while they were crossing the depths on foot over the dry bottom, they were not troubled by the sight of the water rising so near them on both sides, for the sea had been fixed like a wall on both sides.

10.18.2.en: And when Pharaoh and the Egyptians pursued them and went down after them into the sea, in the newly split passage, the walls of water joined together again, and the sea rushed to take its former shape, and became one mass of water (Ex 14:23-31). At that time the Israelites had reached the other bank after the long and wearisome walk in the sea, and then they sang the song of victory to God, who had done a great deed without any shedding of blood on their part, for He destroyed the whole army of the Egyptians in the water, all the horses and the foot soldiers and the chariots.

10.18.3.en: * Who is there who does not know that the Egyptian army, with its horses and chariots and their drivers and its slingers (with slings and bows) and its soldiers armed with heavy weapons and the rest of the enemy's forces in the battle line, are a type of the various passions of the soul that enslave man? For the intellectual impulses and the unrestrained sensual inclinations toward pleasure and pain and greed are exactly like the army we have mentioned. And abuse and insult are like the stones that are hurled with slings, and recklessness is the point of the brandished spear. As for the love of pleasure, it is represented by the horses that draw the chariot with an irresistible impulse.

10.18.4.en: We read in the history in the book of Exodus that the chariot had three men on it who drove it, called "captains," and since you have already learned the mystery of the doorposts and the upper lintel, you understand that these three whom the chariot carries correspond to the threefold division of the soul: the rational, the emotional and the spiritual.

10.18.5.en: The whole army rushes into the water after the Israelites, who went before them in the crossing that was deadly (for the army). Then we find the rod of faith leading the way, and the pillar of cloud giving light, and giving water and life to those who find refuge in it, and destroying their pursuers.

10.18.6.en: The history (the Scripture) teaches us here what kind of people will cross the water and not take with them any of the enemy's army as they come out of the water. For if the enemy came out with them from the water, they would continue in bondage after their coming out, since they would have brought the tyrant with them alive and not drowned him in the water. And if someone wishes to make clear the type in this picture, it is evident that those who pass through the water of holy Baptism must kill the whole army of evil, this army which includes greed and unrestrained desires and thoughts of covetousness and passions of conceit and arrogance, and recklessness, anger, spite and envy and all these things. And since the passions by nature follow our nature, we must kill in the water the base inclinations of the mind and the works that result from them.

10.18.7.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa And therefore the righteous spoiled the ungodly, and praised Your holy name, O Lord.

10.19.0.en: And they praised with one accord Your hand that defended them. [20]

10.19.1.en: The book of Exodus does not mention the fate of Pharaoh's army after it was drowned in the sea. Here he mentions that the corpses, after they sank to the depths, floated above the waters, and the Israelites stripped what was on the dead bodies.

10.19.2.en: This tradition is found in Josephus, namely the Hebrews' taking what the Egyptians who died by drowning in the Red Sea possessed, a matter which is not mentioned in the book of Exodus.

10.19.3.en: * When Pharaoh and the Egyptians pursued them and went down after them into the sea, in the newly split passage, the walls of water joined together again, and the sea rushed to take its former shape, and became one mass of water (Ex 14:23-31). At that time the Israelites had reached the other bank after the long and wearisome walk in the sea, and then they sang the song of victory to God, who had done a great deed without any shedding of blood on their part, for He destroyed the whole army of the Egyptians in the water, all the horses and the foot soldiers and the chariots.

10.20.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa For wisdom opened the mouth of the dumb, and made the tongues of infants plain. [21]

10.20.1.en: It is said in the Targum that some of the children of the Hebrews who were threatened with death in Egypt were carried by angels to the wilderness, and later took part in the journey in the wilderness.

10.20.2.en: Perhaps the children joined the people in the praise (Ex 15).

10.20.3.en: Your love is surpassing, O You who watch over Your people!

10.20.4.en: * You created everything to prepare the palace for Adam my father; You brought him to the garden of Eden as to a royal palace.

10.20.5.en: You loved him and gave him all authority.

10.20.6.en: And when he fell You did not forsake him.

10.20.7.en: You gave him the promise of salvation.

10.20.8.en: You came for his sake and for the sake of his children, and carried the cross of shame for their salvation.

10.20.9.en: Glory to You, O second Adam, Father of mankind!

10.20.10.en: * You sent fire that consumed the sacrifice of Abel; You breathed it in as a sweet savor of pleasure and acceptance.

10.20.11.en: But his wretched brother withdrew from You.

10.20.12.en: So anger ruled over him, and he killed his brother!

10.20.13.en: Grant me not to withdraw my hand from Your hand.

10.20.14.en: Nor to shut the door of my heart before You.

10.20.15.en: So that I may love my brethren, even those who oppose me.

10.20.16.en: * The smell of corruption and abominations spread in the world.

10.20.17.en: And there was no longer any hope of reform, for mankind was treating its Creator with contempt.

10.20.18.en: You looked down from heaven and embraced Noah the righteous.

10.20.19.en: You prepared an ark for him, and You Yourself shut him in.

10.20.20.en: In the midst of the flood Noah was kept in Your heart.

10.20.21.en: In the midst of the total destruction, the ark was an object of admiration to the heavenly ones.

10.20.22.en: Carry me in Your cross, the ark of salvation, for none can rescue me except Your cross, which brings me into the Church, Your holy ship!

10.20.23.en: * The people turned their backs to You; instead of divine wisdom they sought human cunning.

10.20.24.en: They resolved to build a tower whose top would be in heaven, to protect them from a coming, destructive flood!

10.20.25.en: What folly! They were scattered and dispersed.

10.20.26.en: Instead of their rising up to the heavenly, they became warring nations without peace!

10.20.27.en: * In the midst of the whole world Abraham, Your friend, was found.

10.20.28.en: He loved You and possessed You.

10.20.29.en: With joy he wished to offer his only son as a burnt offering.

10.20.30.en: So You raised up from his son a people for Yourself.

10.20.31.en: And You became incarnate of the Virgin Mary, who was of his seed.

10.20.32.en: Glory to You, in whom all the nations are blessed.

10.20.33.en: * In the midst of corrupt Sodom lived Lot and his family.

10.20.34.en: The righteous man tormented his soul with their lawless deeds.

10.20.35.en: He possessed You, so he could not share with them in their evils.

10.20.36.en: And when You brought him out of it and sent down fire upon it, he never thought of looking at it, not even out of curiosity.

10.20.37.en: He lived among them with his heart in isolation from their corruption; how then, after his coming out, would he look at them?

10.20.38.en: His wife deprived herself of You.

10.20.39.en: Her heart returned to Sodom, and she looked behind.

10.20.40.en: She lost all feeling, and became a pillar of salt.

10.20.41.en: She became a statue bearing witness to every soul that is deprived of union with You!

10.20.42.en: In her folly she herself became a testimony to folly and ignorance!

10.20.43.en: * Our father Jacob possessed You and leaned on You.

10.20.44.en: In the midst of his bitter afflictions he found You the cornerstone; he laid his head upon You, and his insight was opened.

10.20.45.en: He saw Your cross as a ladder by which he ascends to heaven.

10.20.46.en: By You the wilderness was turned for him into an open heaven.

10.20.47.en: His brother hated him, so he beheld angels descending to him, accompanying him.

10.20.48.en: And he saw angels ascending with him that he might enjoy You.

10.20.49.en: The bitterness of his soul was turned into surpassing sweetness.

10.20.50.en: * Laban, his uncle and father-in-law, did not possess You, so he set in his heart to take vengeance on Jacob.

10.20.51.en: Instead of the spirit of vengeance, You made of him a witness to Your love and Your work with Jacob!

10.20.52.en: You did not command him to return with his men to where he had been, but You commanded him to meet Jacob, and to bear witness to You that You shepherd him and keep him.

10.20.53.en: How wonderful, for You turn opponents into witnesses to Your love.

10.20.54.en: * You turned Joseph's fetters in the prison into a way of passing over to the throne.

10.20.55.en: The prisoner became the second man in the kingdom.

10.20.56.en: The chief of police stood in amazement.

10.20.57.en: The one who brought him into the prison now asks him for bread for himself and for his household.

10.20.58.en: She who wanted to satisfy the lusts of her body brought him into prison.

10.20.59.en: Now behold, her body needs bread; who will give it to her but he?

10.20.60.en: You made the prisoner a source of satisfaction for all Egypt and for the lands surrounding it.

10.20.61.en: He became a type of You, O Satisfier of souls.

10.20.62.en: You shone upon him that he might perceive Your eternal glory.

10.20.63.en: * You heard the groaning of Your people, and Your bowels yearned over them.

10.20.64.en: You sent them a leader, You kept him for them in the very palace of Pharaoh, You granted that You would speak by his mouth, and You gave him to work wonders and dazzling signs.

10.20.66.en: You shaded them like a cloud by day, and You were a leader to them like a pillar of fire by night. * You brought them through the midst of the sea, and made them pass in a unique procession.

10.20.67.en: But those who rejected You, the way became a tomb for them.

10.20.68.en: They rejected You, O Life, and death swallowed them up.

10.20.69.en: * You turned Your people into a choir of angels.

10.20.70.en: They praise You in the midst of the wilderness, and rejoice because of the abundance of Your love!
